medtop:20000731.definition: The study of the movement and structure of matter, and how it relates to energy

medtop:20000732.label: electromagnetism
medtop:20000732.definition: The study of the physical interactions between electrically charged particles and magnetic fields

medtop:20000733.label: nuclear physics
medtop:20000733.definition: The study of the structure and behaviour of atomic nuclei

medtop:20000734.label: particle physics
medtop:20000734.definition: The study of the nature, properties and interactions of the elementary particles that constitute matter

medtop:20000735.label: scientific research
medtop:20000735.definition: The scientific and methodical investigation of events, procedures and interactions to explain why they occur, or to find solutions for problems

medtop:20000736.label: scientific innovation
medtop:20000736.definition: The development or creation of new scientific or technological products or processes, such as biotech or artificial intelligence applications, robotic limbs or nanoscale cameras

medtop:20000737.label: medical research
medtop:20000737.definition: Investigation conducted in the fields of health and medicine, such as genetic studies, disease research or pharmaceutical drug trials

medtop:20000738.label: scientific exploration
medtop:20000738.definition: Land, sea or space journeys undertaken to discover new information

medtop:20000739.label: space exploration
medtop:20000739.definition: The scientific exploration of outer space through manned and unmanned missions

medtop:20000740.label: scientific publication
medtop:20000740.definition: Academic research findings published in a journal, book or thesis

medtop:20000741.label: scientific institution
medtop:20000741.definition: Institution that carries out or governs scientific work, such as the National Academy of Arts and Sciences

medtop:20000742.label: social sciences
medtop:20000742.definition: The study of human society in such aspects as linguistics, anthropology, economics or sociology

medtop:20000743.label: anthropology
medtop:20000743.definition: The study of human behaviour and social interactions across time

medtop:20000744.label: archaeology
medtop:20000744.definition: The study of human activity throughout time and cultural history, using artefacts left behind by ancient peoples

medtop:20000745.label: economics
medtop:20000745.definition: The study of the laws and principles of economies, such as the production and distribution of goods and services

medtop:20000746.label: geography
medtop:20000746.definition: The study of the physical features of the surface of Earth and its political divisions

medtop:20000747.label: history
medtop:20000747.definition: The study of human events of the past

medtop:20000748.label: information science
medtop:20000748.definition: The study and practice of collecting, classifying, storing, retrieving and disseminating information

medtop:20000749.label: study of law
medtop:20000749.definition: The study of legal systems and the philosophy of law

medtop:20000750.label: linguistics
medtop:20000750.definition: The study of all aspects of human language such as syntax, phonetics, written and spoken forms and variations over time

medtop:20000751.label: philosophy
medtop:20000751.definition: The study of the principles and fundamental questions about matters such as the mind, reason, morality or values

medtop:20000752.label: political science
medtop:20000752.definition: The study of the principles of political and governmental systems, political thought and practices

medtop:20000753.label: psychology
medtop:20000753.definition: The study of the human mind, mental characteristics and emotional processes

medtop:20000754.label: sociology
medtop:20000754.definition: The study of human social organisation, social relationships and societal changes

medtop:20000755.label: scientific standards
medtop:20000755.definition: Nationally or internationally established rules governing scientific and technological study and development, such as calibration standards for scientific tools or equipment

medtop:20000756.label: technology and engineering
medtop:20000756.definition: The study and practice of industrial or applied sciences such as physics, hydrodynamics or thermodynamics

medtop:20000757.label: aerospace engineering
medtop:20000757.definition: The study, design, development and construction of aircraft, spacecraft and missile systems

medtop:20000758.label: rocketry
medtop:20000758.definition: The study, design, development and construction of rockets

medtop:20000759.label: agricultural technology
medtop:20000759.definition: The study and development of techniques and machinery to improve agricultural management and productivity

medtop:20000760.label: civil engineering
medtop:20000760.definition: The study, design, development and construction of structures such as buildings, bridges, tunnels, irrigation and sewage systems, streets or railroads

medtop:20000761.label: electronic engineering
medtop:20000761.definition: The study, design, development and application of systems built on the exchange of electrical charges, such as consumer devices, communications systems or industrial computers

medtop:20000762.label: identification technology
medtop:20000762.definition: The study, development, application and ethical considerations of technological methods for identifying products, animals or people; including radio frequency, biometrics or face recognition

medtop:20000763.label: information technology and computer science
medtop:20000763.definition: The study and design of computer systems, software and networks

medtop:20000764.label: materials science
medtop:20000764.definition: The study of the composition, structure and properties of materials for their use in industry and manufacturing

medtop:20000765.label: micro science
medtop:20000765.definition: The study of and technologies built at a microscopic scale, such as microbiology or microcomputing

medtop:20000766.label: nanotechnology
medtop:20000766.definition: Manipulating objects at the molecular scale

medtop:20000768.label: communities
medtop:20000768.definition: A group of individuals actively sharing a common value or interest

medtop:20000769.label: social networking
medtop:20000769.definition: Social interactions, either in person or online, intended to share information and build relationships around common interests

medtop:20000770.label: demographics
medtop:20000770.definition: The study of human populations and their characteristics, for example statistics or trends around aging populations in a particular geographic region

medtop:20000771.label: immigration
medtop:20000771.definition: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another

medtop:20000772.label: emigration
medtop:20000772.definition: Leaving one's country of residence to settle permanently elsewhere

medtop:20000773.label: illegal immigration
medtop:20000773.definition: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another without legal authorisation from the destination country

medtop:20000774.label: population and census
medtop:20000774.definition: The official count of people living in a given geopolitical area, usually carried out by a governmental body

medtop:20000775.label: discrimination
medtop:20000775.definition: Unfair treatment of, or policies or practices against, individuals or groups of people on the basis of real or perceived membership in a group, such as race, sexual orientation, political or religious beliefs, age or height

medtop:20000776.label: ageism
medtop:20000776.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of age

medtop:20000777.label: racism
medtop:20000777.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of race

medtop:20000778.label: religious discrimination
medtop:20000778.definition: Unfair treatment of individuals or groups of people on the basis of their religious belief

medtop:20000779.label: sexism
medtop:20000779.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people, usually women, on the basis of gender

medtop:20000780.label: family
medtop:20000780.definition: A group of people related genetically or by a legal bond, or who consider themselves part of a familial unit regardless of genetic or legal status

medtop:20000781.label: adoption
medtop:20000781.definition: The legal process of transferring parental rights to someone other than a person's birth parents, that person usually being a child

medtop:20000782.label: Dating and Relationships
medtop:20000782.definition: The development of an intimate connection between individuals, through various forms of activities enjoyed together, often leading to a legal or permanent union such as marriage

medtop:20000783.label: divorce
medtop:20000783.definition: The process by which a marriage is legally dissolved

medtop:20000784.label: family planning
medtop:20000784.definition: Services and education aimed at informing individual decisions about reproduction, such as fertility, in vitro fertilisation, contraception or abortion

medtop:20000785.label: abortion
medtop:20000785.definition: The intentional termination of a pregnancy for elective or medical reasons

medtop:20000786.label: marriage
medtop:20000786.definition: The legal or socially recognised union of individuals, which establishes rights and obligations between them

medtop:20000787.label: parenting
medtop:20000787.definition: The caring for and support of a child's physical, emotional, developmental and social needs from birth to adulthood

medtop:20000788.label: demographic group
medtop:20000788.definition: A subset of society with shared traits

medtop:20000789.label: adults
medtop:20000789.definition: People above an age set by law that entitles them to full liability and certain privileges such as the legal right to drink alcoholic beverages and to vote

medtop:20000790.label: children
medtop:20000790.definition: Young people, usually pre-pubescent, who are legally considered minors and are in a guardianship relationship with adults

medtop:20000791.label: disabilities
medtop:20000791.definition: Physical or mental conditions that limit a person's movements, senses, or activities

medtop:20000792.label: LGBTQ
medtop:20000792.definition: People who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer

medtop:20000793.label: gender
medtop:20000793.definition: The classification of individuals as male, female, or a non-binary designation

medtop:20000794.label: infants
medtop:20000794.definition: Very young people, usually defined as being just born up to the age of two

medtop:20000795.label: national or ethnic minority
medtop:20000795.definition: Groups of people that form a minority on an ethnic or national basis, and their status or issues relating to the majority

medtop:20000796.label: nuclear radiation victims
medtop:20000796.definition: Includes antinuclear movements and compensation for atomic blast victims.

medtop:20000797.label: senior citizens
medtop:20000797.definition: People having passed the age of retirement

medtop:20000798.label: teenagers
medtop:20000798.definition: Young people between the ages that describe childhood and adulthood

medtop:20000799.label: social condition
medtop:20000799.definition: The circumstances or state of affairs affecting a person's life, welfare and relations with others in a society

medtop:20000800.label: homelessness
medtop:20000800.definition: The social condition defined by lack of permanent residence, living in shelters or on streets, and the issues and problems associated with it

medtop:20000801.label: poverty
medtop:20000801.definition: The lack of sufficient resources and means to provide basic needs such as food, clothing or shelter for oneself and one's family

medtop:20000802.label: social problem
medtop:20000802.definition: Issues related to human rights, human welfare and other areas of societal concern

medtop:20000803.label: abusive behaviour
medtop:20000803.definition: Actions that intentionally harm another person or people, often on an ongoing basis, such as psychological or mental abuse, negligence, physical or sexual abuse and torture

medtop:20000804.label: addiction
medtop:20000804.definition: The habitual and compulsive use of substances such as alcohol or drugs, or behaviour such as gambling, gaming or sex, often causing detrimental effects on the body, brain, and relationships with others

medtop:20000805.label: juvenile delinquency
medtop:20000805.definition: Unlawful conduct perpetrated by minors, often on a repeated basis

medtop:20000806.label: prostitution
medtop:20000806.definition: The business of engaging in sexual activity in exchange for payment

medtop:20000807.label: slavery
medtop:20000807.definition: The ownership of people as property, and the involuntary servitude of those people to their owners, which includes unpaid labour and coerced actions

medtop:20000808.label: values
medtop:20000808.definition: A person's or group's principles or standards of behaviour, which guide their way of living and choices made

medtop:20000809.label: corrupt practices
medtop:20000809.definition: Any action which is harmful to others

medtop:20000810.label: death and dying
medtop:20000810.definition: Social, medical and mental health issues relating to people at the end of their lives

medtop:20000811.label: euthanasia
medtop:20000811.definition: The practice of humanely ending the life of a person suffering from a terminal illness

medtop:20000812.label: assisted suicide
medtop:20000812.definition: The practice of assisting a person suffering from a terminal illness in the process of suicide, often with a physician's oversight

medtop:20000813.label: suicide
medtop:20000813.definition: The intentional taking of one's own life

medtop:20000814.label: ethics
medtop:20000814.definition: The moral values and standards that define right and wrong actions or decisions

medtop:20000815.label: pornography
medtop:20000815.definition: The depiction of sexually explicit acts in various media renditions, such as video or photos, often considered obscene or immoral

medtop:20000816.label: sexual behaviour
medtop:20000816.definition: The manner in which people express their sexuality in physical acts

medtop:20000817.label: welfare
medtop:20000817.definition: Help for those in need of food, housing, health and other services

medtop:20000818.label: charity
medtop:20000818.definition: The voluntary giving of money, food or other necessities to those in need

medtop:20000819.label: long-term care
medtop:20000819.definition: Services provided on an extended and ongoing basis to patients suffering from chronic illness or disability

medtop:20000820.label: social services
medtop:20000820.definition: Social programmes, usually publicly sponsored, aimed at promoting people's welfare, such as housing, health care or education services

medtop:20000822.label: competition discipline
medtop:20000822.definition: Different types of sport which can be executed in competitions

medtop:20000823.label: American football
medtop:20000823.definition: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 11 that have offence and defence sections. Each offence attempts to move an oval ball down the 120 yards long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team s end zone.

medtop:20000824.label: archery
medtop:20000824.definition: Archers use bows and arrows to aim at targets 1.22 metres in diameter which are on average 70 metres distant.

medtop:20000825.label: crossbow shooting
medtop:20000825.definition: Shooting with crossbow on targets from different distances

medtop:20000826.label: longbow
medtop:20000826.definition: Shooting with longbow on targets from different distances. The competition is held outdoors on an open (flat) field.

medtop:20000827.label: athletics
medtop:20000827.definition: Competitions involving foot races, jumping and throwing which can be on a track inside a stadium or on outside roads

medtop:20000828.label: cross-country run
medtop:20000828.definition: Competitors run over rough ground and not on a track

medtop:20000829.label: decathlon
medtop:20000829.definition: Individual men's competition which involves accumulating points in 10 different disciplines over two days: 1st day - 100m, long-jump, shot-putt, high-jump, 400m. 2nd day - 110m hurdles, discus, pole-vault, javelin and 1,500 metres.

medtop:20000830.label: discus throw
medtop:20000830.definition: Competitors stand in a netted circle with a 2.50 metres diameter and with a turning motion attempt to throw a discus weighing 2kg for men and 1kg for women as far as possible

medtop:20000831.label: hammer throw
medtop:20000831.definition: Competitors throw a hammer consisting of a metal ball, chain and handle as far as they can from a netted circle which is 2.13 metres in diameter. The hammer weighs 7.26kg for men and 4kg for women

medtop:20000832.label: heptathlon
medtop:20000832.definition: Competition involving seven separate disciplines over two days. 1st day - 100m hurdles, high jump, shot put, 200 metres. 2nd day - long-jump, javelin, 800 metres

medtop:20000833.label: high jump
medtop:20000833.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump as high as possible over a horizontal bar

medtop:20000834.label: hurdles
medtop:20000834.definition: A sprint running race where athletes jump over a series of upright frames

medtop:20000835.label: javelin throw
medtop:20000835.definition: Competitors in a specially-designated throwing area attempt to fling a spear-like javelin as far as possible. The javelin weighs 800 grams for men and 600 grams for women.

medtop:20000836.label: long distance run
medtop:20000836.definition: A running race at distances for more than 1500 metres

medtop:20000837.label: long jump
medtop:20000837.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump in one leap as far as possible

medtop:20000838.label: middle distance run
medtop:20000838.definition: A running race at distances for more than 400 metres and up to and including 1500 metres

medtop:20000839.label: pentathlon
medtop:20000839.definition: Only indoor, 60m hurdles, high jump, shot put, long jump, 800 m

medtop:20000840.label: pole vault
medtop:20000840.definition: Competitors use a flexible pole to propel themselves feet-first into the air and clear a bar which is raised higher at each round of jumps.

medtop:20000841.label: race walking
medtop:20000841.definition: A race requiring the competitor to have always one foot on the ground

medtop:20000842.label: relay run
medtop:20000842.definition: A team of athletes run a relay over identical distances

medtop:20000843.label: shot put
medtop:20000843.definition: Competitors stand in a circle with a 2.13 metres diameter and attempt to throw a metal ball weighing 7.26 kg for men and 4kg for women as far as possible. The longest throw wins.

medtop:20000844.label: sprint run
medtop:20000844.definition: A running race at distances of up to and including 400 metres

medtop:20000845.label: triple jump
medtop:20000845.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then attempt to jump as far forward as they can using a hop, skip and a jump technique.

medtop:20000846.label: Australian rules football
medtop:20000846.definition: A form of football played by two teams of 18 competing on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts. Governed by the Australian Football League.

medtop:20000847.label: badminton
medtop:20000847.definition: Two players or two teams of two compete by hitting a shuttlecock weighing approximately five grams over a high net. The aim for each player/team is to prevent the shuttlecock landing on their side of the court.

medtop:20000848.label: bandy
medtop:20000848.definition: Played outdoors on ice. The size of the ice rink is about the size of a soccer field. Skates like ice hockey. A small hard ball is used for playing. Players play with sticks, much like in ice hockey, but the sticks are shorter and more rounded than in ice

medtop:20000849.label: baseball
medtop:20000849.definition: A game between two teams of nine played on an enclosed ground. The team which scores the most points wins. A point is scored when a player runs around the ground marked out by four bases. To do this he has to hit the ball thrown at him by a rival player.

medtop:20000850.label: rubberball baseball
medtop:20000850.definition: Sometimes called ''soft baseball,'' the game is played with a rubber baseball of varying degrees of hardness depending upon the age and level of the players.

medtop:20000851.label: basketball
medtop:20000851.definition: Game played between two teams of five - points are scored by placing the large inflated ball into a net fixed on a ring 3.05m above the ground.

medtop:20000852.label: biathlon
medtop:20000852.definition: A combination of cross-country skiing and target shooting on a 12.5 K course in a pursuit format.

medtop:20000853.label: billiards
medtop:20000853.definition: A cue sport with balls on a table without a specific order to play them

medtop:20000854.label: bobsleigh
medtop:20000854.definition: One, two or four people racing down a course in a sled that consists of a main hull, a frame, two axles and sets of runners. The total time of all heats in a competition is added together to determine the winner.

medtop:20000855.label: boules
medtop:20000855.definition: Collective name of a number of games where the common goal is to move the competitor's balls as close to a small target ball as possible, played on a grass or sand surface. Balls are thrown (as in petanque and boules) or rolled (as in lawn bowls or bocce).

medtop:20000856.label: boxing
medtop:20000856.definition: Combat sport in which two men/women fight using only their fists covered by padded gloves in a square ring measuring 6m a side. The fight is usually split into 12 rounds of three minutes each.

medtop:20000857.label: bantamweight (boxing)
medtop:20000857.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000858.label: cruiserweight (boxing)
medtop:20000858.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000859.label: featherweight (boxing)
medtop:20000859.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000860.label: flyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000860.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000861.label: heavyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000861.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000862.label: light flyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000862.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000863.label: light-heavyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000863.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000864.label: light-middleweight (boxing)
medtop:20000864.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000865.label: light-welterweight (boxing)
medtop:20000865.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000866.label: lightweight (boxing)
medtop:20000866.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000867.label: middleweight (boxing)
medtop:20000867.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000868.label: straw weight (boxing)
medtop:20000868.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000869.label: super-bantamweight (boxing)
medtop:20000869.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000870.label: super-featherweight (boxing)
medtop:20000870.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000871.label: super-flyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000871.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000872.label: super-heavyweight (boxing)
medtop:20000872.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000873.label: super-middleweight (boxing)
medtop:20000873.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000874.label: welterweight (boxing)
medtop:20000874.definition: Weight category which varies according to the federation or the Olympic Games

medtop:20000875.label: bullfighting
medtop:20000875.definition: Classical contest pitting man against the bull

medtop:20000876.label: Canadian football
medtop:20000876.definition: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 12 that have offence and defence sections. Each offence attempts to move an oval ball down the 150 yards long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team s end zone.

medtop:20000877.label: canoeing
medtop:20000877.definition: Competition involving canoes which are generally kneeled and paddled with a single-bladed paddle

medtop:20000878.label: C1 (canoeing)
medtop:20000878.definition: One-seater canoe (open boat with competitor using a single bladed paddle

medtop:20000879.label: C2 (canoeing)
medtop:20000879.definition: Two-seater canoe (open boat) - competitors use a single bladed paddle

medtop:20000880.label: C4 (canoeing)
medtop:20000880.definition: Four-seater canoe (open boat) with each competitor using a single bladed paddle

medtop:20000881.label: canoe sailing
medtop:20000881.definition: A race involving a canoe equipped with a sail.

medtop:20000882.label: pontoniering
medtop:20000882.definition: Team sport, military tradition, similar to canoe regatta, in boats

medtop:20000883.label: casting (fishing)
medtop:20000883.definition: Using fishing equipment to hit a target and score points

medtop:20000884.label: mountain climbing
medtop:20000884.definition: Moving up mountains using hands and feet

medtop:20000885.label: ice climbing
medtop:20000885.definition: Climbing of ice features such as icefalls and frozen cliffs

medtop:20000887.label: sport climbing
medtop:20000887.definition: Sport climbing as a special category: individual competition, on an artificial wall with time measurement

medtop:20000888.label: cricket
medtop:20000888.definition: Ball sport involving two teams of 11 players, balls, bats and wickets. The aim is to score as many runs as possible, and to get the opposing team 'out'. A 'run' involves a player running between two wickets. The opposing team try to get their rivals 'out'

medtop:20000889.label: croquet
medtop:20000889.definition: Using mallets to hit a ball through hoops

medtop:20000890.label: curling
medtop:20000890.definition: A game played on ice with large flat round stones. A player throws the stone, aiming at a target. Teammates of the player who has thrown the stone can sweep the ice in front of the stone to help smooth its path towards the target.

medtop:20000891.label: icestock sport
medtop:20000891.definition: Similar to curling, played on targets on ice, different stones with straight handle and different rules, played in alpine countries

medtop:20000892.label: cycling
medtop:20000892.definition: A race over a given distance on bicycles.

medtop:20000893.label: artistic cycling
medtop:20000893.definition: Individual or teams on one or two bicycles in an arena. Points are awarded by a jury.

medtop:20000894.label: bi-crossing
medtop:20000894.definition: A race where competitors have to cover a circuit with obstacles as quickly as possible.

medtop:20000895.label: bmx racing
medtop:20000895.definition: Bicycle racing in with inline start and various obstacles over off-road circuits.

medtop:20000896.label: cycle ball
medtop:20000896.definition: Competitive team sport using bicycles. One team against another with two persons per team. The aim is for competitors to move the ball using the front and rear wheels without letting their feet touch the ground.

medtop:20000897.label: cycle sprint race
medtop:20000897.definition: Track cycling race between two cyclists over two or three laps, with a timed sprint finish over the last 200m

medtop:20000898.label: cyclo-cross
medtop:20000898.definition: Staged on various surfaces - earth, grass, sand or tarmac.

medtop:20000899.label: individual pursuit (cycling)
medtop:20000899.definition: Track cycling event where two cyclists set off from midway down opposite straights and try to make up the gap between them

medtop:20000900.label: individual time trial (cycling)
medtop:20000900.definition: A race or stage against the clock with each cyclist setting off individually

medtop:20000901.label: Keirin
medtop:20000901.definition: Sprint between six cyclists where a pacemaker on a moped gradually increases the pace over the first 1400m. When the pacemaker leaves the track the race develops into a sprint finish over the final 6-700m.

medtop:20000902.label: Madison race
medtop:20000902.definition: A points race by teams comprising two cyclists in relay-format

medtop:20000903.label: mountain biking
medtop:20000903.definition: All-terrain, off-road bicycle riding requiring endurance and specially adapted mountain bikes

medtop:20000904.label: points race (cycling)
medtop:20000904.definition: Cyclists aim to complete the highest number of laps. Bonus points are picked up in intermediate sprints held every 2500m

medtop:20000905.label: road cycling
medtop:20000905.definition: Road race with all competitors starting en masse.

medtop:20000906.label: cycling staging race
medtop:20000906.definition: Race disputed by teams with the classifications determined by the combined times over a day

medtop:20000907.label: team cycle sprint
medtop:20000907.definition: A track race where two teams race against each other, starting on opposite sides of the track, following the first lap the first rider pulls away, leaving the second rider to lead the next lap, who then does the same at the last lap, leaving the third rider to finish the race. The team with the fastest time is the winner.

medtop:20000908.label: road cycling team pursuit
medtop:20000908.definition: Track cycle event where two teams set off from midway down opposite straights and try to make up the gap between them

medtop:20000909.label: team time trial (cycling)
medtop:20000909.definition: Teams of cyclists race against the clock

medtop:20000910.label: track race (cycling)
medtop:20000910.definition: A race staged on a track in a velodrome

medtop:20000911.label: competitive dancing
medtop:20000911.definition: Dancing competition where competitors are judged on technique and interpretation.

medtop:20000912.label: darts
medtop:20000912.definition: The sport in which small darts are thrown at a dartboard, a circular target divided into numbered sections.

medtop:20000913.label: diving
medtop:20000913.definition: Competitors dive off a fixed or spring board and are assessed by seven judges giving marks up to ten for their acrobatic moves.

medtop:20000914.label: platform diving
medtop:20000914.definition: Divers take off from a high platform

medtop:20000915.label: springboard diving
medtop:20000915.definition: Divers dive from a high springboard.

medtop:20000916.label: synchronised diving
medtop:20000916.definition: Two competitors from the same team dive off at the same time from separate platforms or springboards. As well as being judged on the standard criteria they are also awarded marks for synchronisation.

medtop:20000917.label: scuba diving
medtop:20000917.definition: Underwater diving with the use of a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus

medtop:20000920.label: oval track dog racing
medtop:20000920.definition: Pursuing an artificial rabbit around an oval track

medtop:20000921.label: dog sled racing
medtop:20000921.definition: Race with dogs harnessed to a sled

medtop:20000922.label: duathlon
medtop:20000922.definition: An athletic event involving running and cycling

medtop:20000923.label: equestrian
medtop:20000923.definition: Horse-based sport disciplines governed by the International Federation for Equestrian Sports, such as dressage, eventing, show jumping and vaulting

medtop:20000924.label: cross-country horse riding
medtop:20000924.definition: Equestrian event held on a designated circuit in the countryside featuring artificial and natural obstacles.

medtop:20000925.label: dressage
medtop:20000925.definition: A rider is judged on a series of moves at three different paces - walk, trot and gallop.

medtop:20000926.label: horse jumping
medtop:20000926.definition: A rider and horse attempt to jump a series of obstacles in an enclosed arena against the clock.

medtop:20000927.label: three day eventing
medtop:20000927.definition: Equestrian event involving three disciplines - Dressage, cross-country and show jumping

medtop:20000928.label: horse driving
medtop:20000928.definition: Equestrian events involving horses being driven in harness, single vehicle around a course.

medtop:20000929.label: fencing
medtop:20000929.definition: Combat sport using a sword or foil.

medtop:20000930.label: epee
medtop:20000930.definition: Category of fencing using a weapon with a triangular cross-section blade and a large bell guard

medtop:20000931.label: foil
medtop:20000931.definition: Category of fencing using a weapon with a rectangular cross-section blade and a small bell guard

medtop:20000932.label: sabre
medtop:20000932.definition: A fencing weapon with a flat blade and knuckle guard used with cutting or thrusting moves

medtop:20000933.label: field hockey
medtop:20000933.definition: A ball sport involving two teams of 11 players using curved sticks. The aim is to score as many goals as possible.

medtop:20000934.label: figure skating
medtop:20000934.definition: To obtain the best marks possible from nine judges who award scores after two prepared sections - both skated to music - during which competitors must attempt to achieve the greatest possible harmony between artistic flair and technical precision.

medtop:20000935.label: ice dance
medtop:20000935.definition: Takes place over three days with, in order, two compulsory dances, the original dance (2min 30sec) and the free dance (4min).

medtop:20000936.label: fist ball
medtop:20000936.definition: Men's team sport similar to volleyball (with a much lower net) executed mainly in gymnastics clubs

medtop:20000937.label: floorball
medtop:20000937.definition: Played indoors in a court the size of a basketball court. 6 players per team, of which one is a goalkeeper. He/she operates kneeling but there is no goal-stick like in ice hockey. The players use plastic clubs and a light plastic ball to pass and shot goal

medtop:20000938.label: flying disc
medtop:20000938.definition: A group of events all played with a flying plastic disc. The exact regulation for the disc is different in different events but it has to be unbroken of solid plastic and a production model with no modification. Flying disc is sometimes called Frisbee.

medtop:20000939.label: Gaelic football
medtop:20000939.definition: A form of football played by two teams of 15 competing on a pitch by running with, kicking and passing a spherical ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts. Governed by the Gaelic Athletic Association.

medtop:20000940.label: golf
medtop:20000940.definition: A game to hit a small hard ball with different clubs around a course of typically 18 holes varying in distance and during a round. The object, depending on the scoring formulae, is to make the fewest strokes possible

medtop:20000941.label: mini golf
medtop:20000941.definition: A game where small hard balls must be holed on an artificial course in as few strokes from the club as possible

medtop:20000942.label: gymnastics
medtop:20000942.definition: A sport consisting of a variety of disciplines in which gymnasts perform artistic and acrobatic moves using different apparatus.

medtop:20000943.label: ball (rhythmic gymnastics)
medtop:20000943.definition: An exercise based on suppleness of the body using a ball.

medtop:20000944.label: beam (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000944.definition: Gymnasts perform leaps and flips from the much feared balance beam just 10 cm wide.

medtop:20000945.label: clubs (rhythmic gymnastics)
medtop:20000945.definition: Dance and gymnastic moves whilst juggling clubs.

medtop:20000946.label: floor exercise (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000946.definition: A gymnastics floor exercise on a 12m/sq matt.

medtop:20000947.label: hoop (rhythmic gymnastics)
medtop:20000947.definition: A hoop is rolled and thrown whilst performing a dance routine.

medtop:20000948.label: horizontal bar (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000948.definition: Gymnasts turn, spin and perform pirouettes around the horizontal bar.

medtop:20000949.label: parallel bars (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000949.definition: Gymnasts swing and turn with guile and grace around the parallel bars.

medtop:20000950.label: pommel horse (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000950.definition: Gymnasts perform an uninterrupted swing motion over a handled horse using balance and strength

medtop:20000951.label: rhythmic gymnastics
medtop:20000951.definition: Mixture of dance and gymnastic moves

medtop:20000952.label: ribbon (rhythmic gymnastics)
medtop:20000952.definition: Gymnasts work through a pre-arranged routine whilst manipulating a spectacular length of ribbon.

medtop:20000953.label: rings (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000953.definition: Gymnasts perform feats of balance and strength from two suspended rings.

medtop:20000954.label: rope (rhythmic gymnastics)
medtop:20000954.definition: Jump and figure movements are performed while a rope is manipulated.

medtop:20000955.label: trampoline
medtop:20000955.definition: Competitors perform complicated twists and turns whilst bouncing on the trampoline.

medtop:20000956.label: uneven bars (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000956.definition: Gymnasts run through an airborne routine swinging around and between the uneven bars.

medtop:20000957.label: vault (artistic gymnastics)
medtop:20000957.definition: Gymnasts propel themselves by jumping on a trampoline after running quickly down a 25m lane

medtop:20000958.label: handball (team)
medtop:20000958.definition: A ball game using the hands contested by two teams of seven trying to throw the ball into the opponents goal.

medtop:20000959.label: hornuss
medtop:20000959.definition: Swiss team sport with 16 or 18 men per team. A rubber puck is hit towards the field of the adversary team which tries to hit the puck in the air with a wooden board thrown in the air

medtop:20000961.label: flat racing
medtop:20000961.definition: A horse race over a flat course.

medtop:20000962.label: harness racing
medtop:20000962.definition: Horses hitched to a jockeyed buggy race round a flat course. Can be performed at a trotting gait or a pacing gait.

medtop:20000963.label: steeple chase
medtop:20000963.definition: A mounted horse race over at least eight classic obstacles, four of which must be different, such as the water jump, spruce fences, mud walls etc.

medtop:20000964.label: hurling
medtop:20000964.definition: A game played by two teams of fifteen each with a curved wooden stick called a hurley. The object is to score a goal by hitting the small ball between the opponents' goalposts either over the crossbar or under it into a net guarded by a goalkeeper.

medtop:20000965.label: ice hockey
medtop:20000965.definition: Two teams of six heavily padded skaters try and outscore each other by hitting a puck into the opponents goal.

medtop:20000966.label: sledge hockey
medtop:20000966.definition: Like ice hockey but instead of skates small sledges are used. Competitors move by pushing with the arms

medtop:20000968.label: Jai Alai (Pelota)
medtop:20000968.definition: A fast ball play using either the bare hand or a wicker scoop in an arena of walls of different outlay and size

medtop:20000970.label: extra lightweight (judo)
medtop:20000970.definition: Up to 60kg for men and 48kg for women.

medtop:20000971.label: half-heavyweight (judo)
medtop:20000971.definition: Up to 100kg for men and 78kg for women.

medtop:20000972.label: half-lightweight (judo)
medtop:20000972.definition: Up to 73kg for men and 57kg for women.

medtop:20000973.label: half-middleweight (judo)
medtop:20000973.definition: Up to 81kg for men and 63kg for women

medtop:20000974.label: heavyweight (judo)
medtop:20000974.definition: Open but usually over 100kg for men and over 78kg for women

medtop:20000975.label: lightweight (judo)
medtop:20000975.definition: Up to 66kg for men and 52kg for women.

medtop:20000976.label: middleweight (judo)
medtop:20000976.definition: Up to 90kg for men and 70kg for women.

medtop:20000977.label: jukendo
medtop:20000977.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a model rifle made of wood. 'Juken' means a rifle or gun with blade (bayonet)

medtop:20000978.label: kabaddi
medtop:20000978.definition: The attacking side scores by touching, and the side to guard scores by capturing. The attacker continues calling it 'kabaddi'.

medtop:20000979.label: kayaking
medtop:20000979.definition: Competition involving kayaks where the paddler sits with their legs facing forward using a double-bladed paddle

medtop:20000980.label: K1 (kayaking)
medtop:20000980.definition: An enclosed boat with the competitor sitting on a fixed seat for one person using a double bladed paddle

medtop:20000981.label: K2 (kayaking)
medtop:20000981.definition: An enclosed boat with the competitor sitting on a fixed seat for two people using double bladed paddles

medtop:20000982.label: K4 (kayaking)
medtop:20000982.definition: An enclosed boat with the competitor sitting on a fixed seat for four people using double bladed paddles

medtop:20000983.label: karate
medtop:20000983.definition: A martial art where chops, punches, kicks and throws are used to defeat an opponent.

medtop:20000984.label: kendo
medtop:20000984.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo sword, sometimes called Japanese fencing

medtop:20000985.label: kyudo
medtop:20000985.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo bow and arrows, sometimes called Japanese archery

medtop:20000986.label: lacrosse
medtop:20000986.definition: Two teams of helmeted and padded players try and outscore each other using a netted stick and hard ball.

medtop:20000987.label: luge
medtop:20000987.definition: Luge (French word for sled) is competed in singles or doubles. The competitor(s) lay on their back on an open sled and race down a course. The competitor(s) and the sled must be in contact when passing the finishing line. The competitor can steer the sled

medtop:20000988.label: marathon
medtop:20000988.definition: A road race where competitors run 42.195km, generally through city streets

medtop:20000989.label: modern pentathlon
medtop:20000989.definition: The Modern Pentathlon comprises five events run over a single day in the following order: shooting, fencing, swimming, horse riding and running.

medtop:20000992.label: endurance race
medtop:20000992.definition: Races for one or more drivers over a long and set distance or time

medtop:20000993.label: F3000
medtop:20000993.definition: Using less powerful motors than the Formula One, designated construction teams race over varied circuits the world over in speed races for individual and team honours over a season.

medtop:20000994.label: Formula One
medtop:20000994.definition: Single cockpit car racing where 20 or so competitors race head to head over varied circuits around the world to win Grand Prix points in an individual and constructors championship

medtop:20000995.label: Indy Racing
medtop:20000995.definition: North American top range professional league speed racing over circuits.

medtop:20000997.label: motor car rallying
medtop:20000997.definition: A season of endurance races over closed circuits including dirt tracks, roads and even snowy conditions featuring specials using adapted road cars with a driver and co-pilot.

medtop:20000998.label: motorcycling
medtop:20000998.definition: Races with 2, 3 or 4 wheels vehicles with a saddle and handlebars

medtop:20000999.label: motorcycle endurance
medtop:20000999.definition: A road race of consistency and endurance

medtop:20001000.label: enduro
medtop:20001000.definition: A race of speed, endurance and regularity over varied surfaces such as through forests and on dirt tracks

medtop:20001002.label: moto-ball
medtop:20001002.definition: Team sport where drivers play a ball

medtop:20001003.label: moto-cross
medtop:20001003.definition: Raced over dirt tracks featuring severe mounds

medtop:20001006.label: side-cars
medtop:20001006.definition: Of different engine sizes but attached to a side car featuring a passenger

medtop:20001007.label: speedway
medtop:20001007.definition: Race involving up to six riders competing over a flat oval track. Speedway motorcycles use only one gear and have no brakes

medtop:20001008.label: motorcycling trial
medtop:20001008.definition: A race of consistency and endurance over varied terrain

medtop:20001009.label: naginata
medtop:20001009.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a pole sword made of wood. 'Naginata' means a spear with a curved blade

medtop:20001010.label: netball
medtop:20001010.definition: A woman's sport similar to basketball though without a board behind the basket

medtop:20001011.label: orienteering
medtop:20001011.definition: An individual time-trial over a route marked out by beacons. The competitor has to search out and find in a specific order. The contestant makes his way with the help of a compass and map

medtop:20001012.label: ski orienteering
medtop:20001012.definition: An individual ski time-trial over a route marked out by beacons, that the competitor has to search out and find in a specific order. The contestant makes his way with the help of a compass and map

medtop:20001013.label: parachuting
medtop:20001013.definition: Jumping from an aeroplane using a parachute, competitions are precision landings, voltige, individual and team

medtop:20001014.label: polo
medtop:20001014.definition: With the aid of a mallet two teams of four horsemen try and knock a bamboo ball into the opponents goal over a pitch 250m long and 150m wide. The game is divided into 4, 6, or 8 time periods of 7min 30sec called chukkas.

medtop:20001015.label: pool
medtop:20001015.definition: A cue sport on a table with pockets, played with different numbers of balls

medtop:20001016.label: power boating
medtop:20001016.definition: Races between motor boats on rivers or lakes

medtop:20001017.label: rodeo
medtop:20001017.definition: A discipline where wild horses or bulls must be mounted and mastered

medtop:20001025.label: roller hockey
medtop:20001025.definition: Team sport similar to ice hockey, executed on 4 wheel roller skates with sticks and a ball

medtop:20001026.label: rowing
medtop:20001026.definition: Boat racing usually on flat calm waters with boats for 1, 2, 4 or 8 rowers

medtop:20001027.label: coxed four
medtop:20001027.definition: Four person boats with just one oar each and with a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001028.label: coxed pair
medtop:20001028.definition: Two person boats with just one oar each and with a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001029.label: coxless four
medtop:20001029.definition: Four person boats with just one oar each and without a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001030.label: coxless pair
medtop:20001030.definition: Two person boats with just one oar each and without a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001031.label: double sculls
medtop:20001031.definition: Two person boats with two oars each

medtop:20001032.label: coxed eight
medtop:20001032.definition: Eight person boats with just one oar each and with a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001033.label: quadruple sculls
medtop:20001033.definition: Four person boats with two oars each and without a team mate to give directions

medtop:20001034.label: single sculls
medtop:20001034.definition: Single person boats with two oars

medtop:20001035.label: rugby league
medtop:20001035.definition: A type of rugby where two teams of 13 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts. Governed by Rugby League International Federation.

medtop:20001036.label: rugby union
medtop:20001036.definition: A type of rugby where two teams of 15 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts. Governed by the World Rugby organization.

medtop:20001037.label: rugby sevens
medtop:20001037.definition: A type of rugby union where two teams of 7 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts. Governed by the World Rugby organization.

medtop:20001038.label: sailing
medtop:20001038.definition: Sailing boat racing over a route

medtop:20001040.label: dinghy
medtop:20001040.definition: Single hulled vessel without a fixed keel

medtop:20001041.label: keelboat
medtop:20001041.definition: Single hulled vessel with a fixed keel

medtop:20001043.label: ocean sailing
medtop:20001043.definition: Sailing vessels across oceans as part of a competitive race.

medtop:20001044.label: round the world race
medtop:20001044.definition: Sailing vessels around the world as a race

medtop:20001045.label: solo ocean sailing
medtop:20001045.definition: Sailing oceans as an individual, as part of a race.

medtop:20001046.label: non-stop solo race
medtop:20001046.definition: Races either clockwise or anti clockwise around the globe without stopping at any ports between start and finish of race.

medtop:20001047.label: sepak takraw
medtop:20001047.definition: A game like volleyball where hands must not be used, using a ball made of rattan

medtop:20001048.label: shinty
medtop:20001048.definition: A ball game involving 2 teams with curved sticks called camans. The object is to score goals by hitting the small leather ball through the goals.

medtop:20001049.label: sport shooting
medtop:20001049.definition: Precision sport using a hand gun, rifle or shotgun

medtop:20001052.label: running target shooting
medtop:20001052.definition: Shooting event with an airgun and a target that moves sideways

medtop:20001054.label: clay pigeon shooting
medtop:20001054.definition: Shooting event which involves shooting at special flying targets, known as clay pigeons or clay targets

medtop:20001055.label: skeleton
medtop:20001055.definition: In skeleton the competitor lies on his/her stomach when racing down the course. The competitor must be on the sled when crossing the finishing line.

medtop:20001056.label: skiing
medtop:20001056.definition: A winter sport using different types of skis

medtop:20001057.label: alpine skiing
medtop:20001057.definition: Racing downhill on snow-covered slopes using alpine techniques and equipment. The slopes contain intermediate gates which are spaced according to the discipline involved.

medtop:20001058.label: freestyle skiing
medtop:20001058.definition: Skiing competitions which, in contrast to alpine skiing, incorporate acrobatic moves and jumps. Events include aerials, halfpipe, slopestyle, ski cross, moguls and big air.

medtop:20001059.label: grass skiing
medtop:20001059.definition: Alpine skiing on roller skis and grass

medtop:20001060.label: Nordic skiing
medtop:20001060.definition: Practiced in relatively-flat, snowy countryside and based on power and endurance.

medtop:20001061.label: ski jumping
medtop:20001061.definition: Competitors descend a snow covered elevated ramp on skis and try to fly off it as far as possible, receiving marks for distance, style of flight and landing

medtop:20001062.label: sky diving
medtop:20001062.definition: Parachuting competitions with long distance falls without using a parachute

medtop:20001063.label: snooker
medtop:20001063.definition: A cue sport with balls on a table to be potted in a specific order

medtop:20001064.label: snowboarding
medtop:20001064.definition: Practiced with a single board (rather than two skis)

medtop:20001065.label: football
medtop:20001065.definition: Also known as soccer. Played by two teams competing on a pitch by kicking a spherical ball. Points are scored by kicking or heading the ball into a goal. Governed by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association

medtop:20001066.label: softball
medtop:20001066.definition: Similar to baseball but with a larger and softer ball, a thinner bat, shorter gaps between bases and less innings

medtop:20001067.label: speed skating
medtop:20001067.definition: Timed races competed by two or more skaters at a time on an oval ice track

medtop:20001068.label: squash
medtop:20001068.definition: A racquet sport of strategy and endurance played by singles or doubles teams in a walled court with a small rubber ball

medtop:20001069.label: sumo wrestling
medtop:20001069.definition: A combat sport of speed and rapidity with much ceremony where two contestants try to throw or slap a competitor out of a marked area. Generally practiced in Japan by large men.

medtop:20001070.label: surfing
medtop:20001070.definition: Water sport where contestants catch and ride waves upright on a surfboard

medtop:20001071.label: swimming
medtop:20001071.definition: A water sport where contestants swim as fast as possible in a given style and win races by being the first to touch home

medtop:20001072.label: backstroke
medtop:20001072.definition: Swimming style, on the back, legs move in flapping motion whilst arms propel the swimmer forward

medtop:20001073.label: breaststroke
medtop:20001073.definition: Swimming style , on the front, effecting forward and outward push movements with the arms and backward and outward pushes with the legs

medtop:20001074.label: butterfly swimming
medtop:20001074.definition: Swimming style , swum on the front with the shoulders remaining parallel to the water both arms moving in simultaneous windmill fashion, the legs remain together and are moved in a flapping motion. The most physical of all styles.

medtop:20001075.label: freestyle swimming
medtop:20001075.definition: Any swimming style may be employed, though front crawl is universally employed

medtop:20001076.label: medley swimming
medtop:20001076.definition: A combination of four different swimming styles in one race

medtop:20001077.label: marathon swimming
medtop:20001077.definition: A long distance open water swimming

medtop:20001078.label: relay freestyle swimming
medtop:20001078.definition: Team of swimmers swim a relay in the swimming style of their choice

medtop:20001079.label: relay medley swimming
medtop:20001079.definition: Team relay race involving a combination of four different swimming styles

medtop:20001080.label: short course swimming
medtop:20001080.definition: Races competed in a 25m length pool

medtop:20001081.label: synchronised free routine
medtop:20001081.definition: In the free programme, music, movements and their order of execution are not restricted.

medtop:20001082.label: synchronised technical routine
medtop:20001082.definition: Contestants obtain points from 10 sitting judges by executing certain synchronised artistic shapes and movements in the water. In the technical programme, competitors must execute a range of specific moves in a given order.

medtop:20001083.label: table tennis
medtop:20001083.definition: A racquet sport for two or four (in doubles), who compete at a table divided by a net using a small bat to play a lightweight ball

medtop:20001084.label: Taekwon-Do
medtop:20001084.definition: A martial art of Korean origin

medtop:20001085.label: tennis
medtop:20001085.definition: A sport where two players, four in doubles, equipped with a racket compete by hitting the ball over a net into the opponent's side of the court with the aim of putting it out of reach within the regulation lines, thus winning points.

medtop:20001086.label: ten pin bowling
medtop:20001086.definition: A game in which a player scores points by trying to knock down ten 'pins' using a ball - if unsuccessful the player has a second attempt. A game consists of ten frames.

medtop:20001087.label: triathlon
medtop:20001087.definition: An endurance multi-sport where competitors first swim, then cycle and then run a road race. Distances vary according to the competition.

medtop:20001088.label: tug-of-war
medtop:20001088.definition: Two teams pulling against each other on a rope

medtop:20001089.label: volleyball
medtop:20001089.definition: Two teams of six record points by hitting a ball over a net into the opponent's half of the court, keeping it in the air at all times. Points are won when opponents fail to return the ball.

medtop:20001090.label: beach volleyball
medtop:20001090.definition: Two teams of two players compete on a sand court. Unlike indoor volleyball, points are scored only when the serving team wins a rally or forces an error. The sand surface makes it more physically demanding than volleyball

medtop:20001091.label: water polo
medtop:20001091.definition: Played in a pool between two teams of 7, who must stay afloat and can only use one hand to pass the ball or swim with it before trying to throw it into the opponents net to score goals.

medtop:20001092.label: water skiing
medtop:20001092.definition: On one or two skis contestants are pulled by a power boat along the water's surface

medtop:20001093.label: weightlifting and powerlifting
medtop:20001093.definition: A strength test where competitors lift as heavy a weight as possible

medtop:20001094.label: clean and jerk (weightlifting)
medtop:20001094.definition: The bar is first lifted to the shoulders and then jerk it above the head and keep it there while maintaining straight legs

medtop:20001095.label: powerlifting
medtop:20001095.definition: A strength test where competitors lift as heavy a weight as possible

medtop:20001096.label: snatch (weightlifting)
medtop:20001096.definition: The bar must be lifted from floor to above the head in one movement

medtop:20001097.label: windsurfing
medtop:20001097.definition: Contestants must complete a marked out course as fast as possible on a windsurf board

medtop:20001098.label: wrestling
medtop:20001098.definition: Combat sport where each wrestler attempts to win over his adversary, by holding both shoulders on the ground (fall) long enough to be in control. Points can also be decisive.

medtop:20001099.label: freestyle wrestling
medtop:20001099.definition: A style where leg holds are allowed

medtop:20001100.label: greco-roman
medtop:20001100.definition: A style where the only holds allowed are those between the head and the belt

medtop:20001101.label: Swiss wrestling
medtop:20001101.definition: Traditional Swiss sport similar to wrestling with specific rules

medtop:20001103.label: disciplinary action in sport
medtop:20001103.definition: Actions, including fines and suspensions levied by sports organisations and teams

medtop:20001104.label: drug use in sport
medtop:20001104.definition: Drug use associated with sport activities, including doping, abuse, testing and permitted medical uses

medtop:20001105.label: drug abuse in sport
medtop:20001105.definition: Using drugs to improve competitiveness in sports

medtop:20001106.label: drug testing in sport
medtop:20001106.definition: Means and ways to check the use of drugs in sports

medtop:20001107.label: medical drug use in sport
medtop:20001107.definition: Use of drugs for medical reasons as permitted by sport regulators

medtop:20001108.label: sport event
medtop:20001108.definition: An event featuring one or more sport competitions

medtop:20001109.label: continental championship
medtop:20001109.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from countries from one continent may participate. Called a *Championship*

medtop:20001110.label: continental cup
medtop:20001110.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from countries from one continent may participate. Called a *Cup*

medtop:20001111.label: continental games
medtop:20001111.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from countries from one continent may participate. Called *Games*

medtop:20001112.label: international championship
medtop:20001112.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from different countries may participate. Called a *Championship*

medtop:20001113.label: international cup
medtop:20001113.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from different countries may participate. Called a *Cup*

medtop:20001114.label: international games
medtop:20001114.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from different countries may participate. Called *Games*

medtop:20001115.label: national championship
medtop:20001115.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from one country may participate. Called a *Championship*

medtop:20001116.label: national cup
medtop:20001116.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from one country may participate. Called a *Cup*

medtop:20001117.label: national games
medtop:20001117.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from one country may participate. Called *Games*

medtop:20001118.label: regional championship
medtop:20001118.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from a region of a country may participate. Called a *Championship*

medtop:20001119.label: regional cup
medtop:20001119.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from a region of a country may participate. Called a *Cup*

medtop:20001120.label: regional games
medtop:20001120.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from a region of a country may participate. Called *Games*

medtop:20001121.label: world championship
medtop:20001121.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from the five continents may participate. Called *World Championship*

medtop:20001122.label: world cup
medtop:20001122.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from the five continents may participate. Called *World Cup*

medtop:20001123.label: world games
medtop:20001123.definition: A competition where individuals or teams from the five continents may participate. Called *World Games*

medtop:20001125.label: sport organisation
medtop:20001125.definition: Organisations or associations that govern sports

medtop:20001126.label: sport venue
medtop:20001126.definition: Gymnasiums, stadiums, arenas or facilities where sports events take place

medtop:20001128.label: weather forecast
medtop:20001128.definition: The long- or short-term meteorological prediction and reporting of the upcoming weather for a given region

medtop:20001129.label: weather phenomena
medtop:20001129.definition: Short- or long-term meteorological phenomena worthy of study, reporting or public advisory such as climate change, storms, heat waves or tornadoes

medtop:20001130.label: weather statistic
medtop:20001130.definition: Numerical facts about the weather such as temperature, barometric pressure, river levels, humidity or high and low tides

medtop:20001131.label: weather warning
medtop:20001131.definition: Alerts issued to the public about severe or notable weather in their area

medtop:20001132.label: cultural policy
medtop:20001132.definition: Government policies related to the promotion and support of the arts

medtop:20001133.label: musical
medtop:20001133.definition: A genre of music theatre in which singing and dancing play an essential part of the storytelling

medtop:20001134.label: operetta
medtop:20001134.definition: A genre of music theatre that usually has a light or humorous theme where some of the libretto is usually spoken rather than sung.

medtop:20001135.label: art exhibition
medtop:20001135.definition: Temporary presentation of art in museums, art halls or galleries

medtop:20001136.label: trade show or expo
medtop:20001136.definition: Market place to display and trade goods or services

medtop:20001137.label: stock recommendation
medtop:20001137.definition: An analyst's recommendation for particular stocks. May include the analyst s price target for the stock.

medtop:20001138.label: buy recommendation
medtop:20001138.definition: An analyst's recommendation to buy particular stocks. May include the analyst s price target for the stock.

medtop:20001139.label: hold recommendation
medtop:20001139.definition: An analyst's recommendation to hold particular stocks. May include the analyst s price target for the stock.

medtop:20001140.label: sell recommendation
medtop:20001140.definition: An analyst's recommendation to sell particular stocks. May include the analyst s price target for the stock.

medtop:20001141.label: hot stock
medtop:20001141.definition: Remarkable price movements of a particular stock.

medtop:20001142.label: recreational hiking and climbing
medtop:20001142.definition: Sportive activities in the mountains including climbing and hiking

medtop:20001143.label: party
medtop:20001143.definition: A social gathering of invited guests, often involving eating, drinking, dancing or the playing of games

medtop:20001144.label: civilian service
medtop:20001144.definition: Unpaid service for the community as civilian

medtop:20001145.label: military service
medtop:20001145.definition: Service by an individual in an army or militia. Service may be on a volunteer basis or a result of an involuntary draft or government requirement.

medtop:20001146.label: integration policy
medtop:20001146.definition: Improving the co-existence of groups of the society

medtop:20001147.label: sports policies
medtop:20001147.definition: Government policies regulating sports, including sports betting, performance enhancing drug laws and the promition of sports to children for health purposes

medtop:20001148.label: sports transaction
medtop:20001148.definition: The transfer of an athlete from one team to another, the hiring or drafting of an athlete onto a team or the change in professional status of a player on a team

medtop:20001149.label: cross-country skiing
medtop:20001149.definition: Nordic ski race competed in relatively-flat, snowy countryside on narrow skis.

medtop:20001150.label: Nordic combined
medtop:20001150.definition: Competition combining cross-country skiing and ski jumping

medtop:20001151.label: short track speed skating
medtop:20001151.definition: Races competed by four or more skaters at a time on a small oval ice track

medtop:20001152.label: artistic gymnastics
medtop:20001152.definition: Gymnasts perform artistic and acrobatic moves on different apparatus. There are 6 events for men and 4 for women

medtop:20001153.label: Telemark skiing
medtop:20001153.definition: Races combining downhill and cross-country skiing events with unique Telemark techniques and equipment.

medtop:20001154.label: chess
medtop:20001154.definition: Competition between two players using a chequered board with 16 pieces to each side, each with specific ranges of movement depending on their identity

medtop:20001155.label: roller sports
medtop:20001155.definition: Various competitions using wheeled equipment such as roller skates, inline skates, and skateboards.

medtop:20001156.label: skateboarding
medtop:20001156.definition: Competitions involving stunts and acrobatic feats performed on a skateboard using various ramps and other obstacles

medtop:20001157.label: martial arts
medtop:20001157.definition: Martial arts are codified systems and traditions of combat practices, which are practiced for a variety of reasons: self-defence, competition, physical health and fitness, entertainment, as well as mental, physical, and spiritual development.

medtop:20001158.label: start-up and entrepreneurial business
medtop:20001158.definition: The process of designing, launching and running a new business

medtop:20001159.label: public contract
medtop:20001159.definition: Written contracts between companies and public authorities for the execution of works, the supply of products or the provision of services.

medtop:20001160.label: handicrafts
medtop:20001160.definition: The creators and sellers of crafts and the making and selling of the supplies used to make those crafts

medtop:20001161.label: Internet of Things
medtop:20001161.definition: A network of devices using microchips, electronic sensors and communication by the Internet

medtop:20001162.label: asset management
medtop:20001162.definition: Managing investments on behalf of others

medtop:20001163.label: client relationship management
medtop:20001163.definition: Creating and maintaining a relationship with the customers to increase sales.

medtop:20001164.label: payment service
medtop:20001164.definition: Services for executing payments including cash, cheque, credit card, debit card, direct debit, electronic funds transfer, internet banking, electronic and mobile payment.

medtop:20001165.label: capital goods
medtop:20001165.definition: Durable goods used in the production of other goods or services.

medtop:20001166.label: railway manufacturing
medtop:20001166.definition: Manufactures of rolling stock and suppliers for the maintenance and repair of railroads

medtop:20001167.label: medical equipment
medtop:20001167.definition: Manufacture of medical and surgical devices for diagnosis and treatment such as optical and imaging equipment

medtop:20001168.label: pet product and service
medtop:20001168.definition: Hygiene products, care and nutrition for pets

medtop:20001169.label: e-cigarette
medtop:20001169.definition: An electronic cigarette is a battery-operated device with an atomizer and a cartridge containing either a nicotine or a non-nicotine liquid solution.

medtop:20001170.label: logistics
medtop:20001170.definition: Supply chain, inventory management and transportation of products.

medtop:20001171.label: sharing economy
medtop:20001171.definition: Peer-to-peer-based sharing of access to goods and services

medtop:20001172.label: small and medium enterprise
medtop:20001172.definition: A small and medium enterprise (SME) is a company whose number of employees, balance and turnover cannot exceed certain limits set by the country where it is located

medtop:20001173.label: regulatory authority
medtop:20001173.definition: Authority responsible for the regulation or supervision of a business sector.

medtop:20001174.label: regional development policy
medtop:20001174.definition: Government or private policies, such as business incentives, aimed at the development of a region

medtop:20001175.label: artistic swimming
medtop:20001175.definition: A sport in which swimmers, in solo, duet or team configurations, perform coordinated or identical movements in time to music. They are judged and are awarded points for body position, control, and the degree of difficulty of the moves.

medtop:20001176.label: rugby
medtop:20001176.definition: A form of football developed in Rugby (England) played with an oval ball that may be kicked, carried and passed from hand to hand. Points are scored when one team carries the ball over the other team's goal line or kicks the ball between two goal posts.

medtop:20001177.label: Olympic Games
medtop:20001177.definition: Games organised by the International Olympic Committee and held each 4 years in summer or winter.

medtop:20001178.label: Paralympic Games
medtop:20001178.definition: Games for disabled athletes organised by the International Paralympic Committee and held each 4 years in winter or summer

medtop:20001179.label: series
medtop:20001179.definition: A connected set of fictional or non-fictional program episodes that run under the same title.

medtop:20001180.label: drama (theatre)
medtop:20001180.definition: A genre of theatre where dramatic or comedic plays are performed on the stage

medtop:20001181.label: festival
medtop:20001181.definition: Events showcasing artistic endeavours, often regularly occurring, such as dance, music, theatre, poetry or comedy festivals

medtop:20001182.label: social media
medtop:20001182.definition: Content created to be shared within online social networks

medtop:20001183.label: eSports
medtop:20001183.definition: Competitions involving video games played by professional gamers

medtop:20001184.label: hip hop
medtop:20001184.definition: A genre of music developed in African American communities in the United States in the 1970s which consists of rapping usually with an electronic backing

medtop:20001185.label: r&b
medtop:20001185.definition: A genre of music originated in African American communities in the 1940s and featuring soulful vocals

medtop:20001186.label: heavy metal
medtop:20001186.definition: A genre of loud, aggressive rock music that was developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s

medtop:20001187.label: dance band music
medtop:20001187.definition: A Swedish genre of music characterized by music inspired by swing, schlager, country, jazz and rock that is often danced to in pairs

medtop:20001188.label: electronic dance music
medtop:20001188.definition: A genre of music that employs electronic instruments and is primarily made for nightclubs, raves, and festivals

medtop:20001189.label: children's music
medtop:20001189.definition: A genre of music featuring songs composed and performed for children

medtop:20001190.label: stand-up comedy
medtop:20001190.definition: A comic style in which a comedian performs a series of jokes or stories in front of a live audience, usually speaking directly to them

medtop:20001191.label: cabaret
medtop:20001191.definition: A form of theatrical entertainment featuring music, song, dance, recitation, or drama that is performed in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience eats or drinks at tables

medtop:20001192.label: influencers
medtop:20001192.definition: Persons who distribute content on internet forums and social media and are followed by many people thereby influencing them to buy and use products

medtop:20001193.label: sexual misconduct
medtop:20001193.definition: Unwanted behaviour of a sexual nature that is of lesser offense than felony sexual assault, particularly when behaviour occurs in a normally non-sexual situation, or where there is some aspect of personal power or authority involved

medtop:20001194.label: accounting crime
medtop:20001194.definition: The intentional misrepresentation or alteration of accounting records regarding sales, revenues, expenses and other factors

medtop:20001195.label: tax evasion
medtop:20001195.definition: The illegal evasion of taxes by individuals, corporations, and trusts

medtop:20001196.label: reckless driving
medtop:20001196.definition: Serious traffic violations that are likely to, or have led to, the endangerment, injury or death of a person or persons, or the endangerment of or significant property damage

medtop:20001197.label: administrative law
medtop:20001197.definition: Body of law that governs the actions of governmental administrative agencies

medtop:20001198.label: court-ordered psychiatric treatment
medtop:20001198.definition: Psychiatric treatment imposed upon persons with mental health conditions in prisons and jails or as a condition of probation, supervision or parole

medtop:20001199.label: suspended sentence
medtop:20001199.definition: Legal arrangement where a judge delays the serving of a sentence by a person who has been found guilty of a crime in order to give them a probationary period

medtop:20001200.label: dropped criminal investigation
medtop:20001200.definition: When police and/or prosecutors end an investigation without a conclusion

medtop:20001202.label: wildfire
medtop:20001202.definition: An uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation

medtop:20001203.label: textile arts
medtop:20001203.definition: Arts and crafts that use plant, animal, or synthetic fibres to construct practical or decorative object

medtop:20001204.label: woodworking
medtop:20001204.definition: The activity or skill of making items, such as furniture or cabinets, from wood

medtop:20001205.label: forging
medtop:20001205.definition: The shaping of metal using localized compressive forces, such as heating and hammering

medtop:20001206.label: self-employment
medtop:20001206.definition: A situation in which an individual works for themselves as a freelancer or business owner instead of working for an employer that pays a salary or a wage

medtop:20001207.label: biofuel
medtop:20001207.definition: Fuel that is derived from biomass, such as ethanol

medtop:20001208.label: geothermal power
medtop:20001208.definition: Thermal energy that is generated and stored in the Earth

medtop:20001209.label: solar power
medtop:20001209.definition: Electricity generated and harvested from the sun's rays

medtop:20001210.label: hydroelectric power
medtop:20001210.definition: Electricity produced from hydropower when water flows through turbines

medtop:20001211.label: wind power
medtop:20001211.definition: Electricity that is generated by kinetic energy of wind, usually produced by windmills or turbines

medtop:20001212.label: religious school
medtop:20001212.definition: School that has a religious component in its operations or its curriculum

medtop:20001213.label: state school
medtop:20001213.definition: Schools maintained by public funds, usually government-imposed taxes

medtop:20001214.label: private school
medtop:20001214.definition: Schools maintained by private funds and organisations

medtop:20001215.label: independent school
medtop:20001215.definition: Schools funded by money from taxes via government, but run by companies, organisations or cooperatives

medtop:20001216.label: vocational education
medtop:20001216.definition: Education that provides students with practical experience and training in a particular occupational field. It is sometimes referred to as career education or technical education

medtop:20001217.label: educational grading
medtop:20001217.definition: The evaluation of a student's achievement on a test, assignment or course and the policies and methods around assigning those grades

medtop:20001218.label: pandemic
medtop:20001218.definition: An epidemic of infectious disease that has spread across a large region or even worldwide

medtop:20001219.label: drug rehabilitation
medtop:20001219.definition: Medical or psychotherapeutic treatment for dependency on substances such as alcohol, prescription and controlled drugs

medtop:20001220.label: general practice
medtop:20001220.definition: The treatment of a wide range of acute and long-term medical conditions and symptoms

medtop:20001221.label: emergency care
medtop:20001221.definition: Immediate care of patients with critical medical emergencies, either inside or outside of a hospital

medtop:20001222.label: orthopaedics
medtop:20001222.definition: A medical specialisation that focuses on conditions involving the musculoskeletal system

medtop:20001223.label: oncology
medtop:20001223.definition: A medical specialisation that focuses on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer

medtop:20001224.label: radiology
